declared.title: Divergent consequences of success and failure in Japan and North America: An investigation of self-improving motivations and malleable selves.
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « divergent consequences of success and failure in Japan and North America self-improving motivations » (2026-11-23)

population: Japanese and North American participants in 4 studies; sizes not given in the abstract

findings.text: North Americans who failed on a task persisted less on a follow-up task than those who succeeded

support.sentence: Replicating past research, North Americans who failed on a task persisted less on a follow-up task than those who succeeded.

findings.text: Japanese who failed on a task persisted more on the follow-up task than those who succeeded

support.sentence: In contrast, Japanese who failed persisted more than those who succeeded.

findings.text: The cultural difference came at least partly from different beliefs about whether effort pays

support.sentence: Study 3 unpackaged the cultural differences by demonstrating that they are due, at least in part, to divergent lay theories regarding the utility of effort.

limits: persistence on the next task, not learning nor later success
2 cultures only, no Arab sample; culture itself is not assigned (the cultural difference is an association)
2001: an old study of 2 cultures; no later test with an Arab sample found
how failure was produced (real or false feedback) is not said in the abstract; full text not read
